en.title: Metroid Ravenous Announced for Switch 2, A Sequel to Dread
en.summary: Samus Aran's next 2D adventure, Metroid Ravenous, has been officially revealed for the Nintendo Switch 2. It's a direct sequel to the critically acclaimed Metroid Dread.
en.body:
The galaxy's most formidable bounty hunter is back in a brand new 2D adventure. Nintendo has officially announced **Metroid Ravenous**, a direct sequel to the highly successful **Metroid Dread**, set to launch on January 28, 2027, exclusively for the **Nintendo Switch 2**. This revelation came during a recent Nintendo Direct broadcast, sending ripples of excitement through the Metroid fanbase.

A trailer offered a glimpse into the perilous journey awaiting Samus, showcasing her facing off against strange, energy-draining adversaries. Her chilling response, "It's eat or be eaten," perfectly encapsulates the tone and hints at new survival mechanics. The title itself, **Metroid Ravenous**, previously surfaced through a quickly removed Brazilian ratings board listing, sparking speculation that it was connected to **Metroid Dread's** antagonist, Raven Beak – a theory now seemingly confirmed.

This latest installment appears to be once again in the capable hands of **MercurySteam**, the Spanish development studio renowned for their work on **Metroid Dread** and **Metroid: Samus Returns**. Their collaboration with Nintendo on **Metroid Dread** was met with widespread critical acclaim, with IGN praising its blend of exploration, progression, modern combat, and exceptional boss fights, awarding it a 9/10. For those keeping track, the 2D side-scrolling Metroid saga, which includes **Ravenous** and **Dread**, continues years after the events of the more recent **Metroid Prime 4**, so direct narrative links to that first-person entry are unlikely.

## A Ravenous Appetite for More Metroid

The announcement has ignited passionate discussions among fans, eager to see how **MercurySteam** will build upon the foundation of **Metroid Dread**. The subtitle "Ravenous" has particularly fueled speculation. Many are theorizing that it could tie into the Metroid suit Samus acquires at the end of **Dread**, perhaps introducing a mechanic where she must consume enemies to sustain her energy. This would add a fresh layer of survival horror to the series' signature exploration and combat.

The return of a 2D Metroid game, especially a sequel to a title that revitalized the classic formula, is precisely what many fans have been clamoring for. After the long wait for **Metroid Dread** and the somewhat uncertain future of the **Metroid Prime** series, **Metroid Ravenous** represents a significant win for the franchise's dedicated community, promising more of the challenging gameplay and atmospheric world-building they adore.

## What's Next

With a release date set for January 28, 2027, **Metroid Ravenous** is still some time away. Further details regarding gameplay specifics, story elements, and potential new abilities are expected to be revealed closer to launch. Fans will be eagerly awaiting more glimpses of Samus's next harrowing mission.

content_raw: Samus Aran will return in Metroid Ravenous, a side-scrolling sequel to Metroid Dread . Announced during today's Nintendo Direct broadcast, Metroid Ravenous will launch for Switch 2 on January 28, 2027. A trailer revealed Samus being attacked by strange enemies who zapped her energy. "It's eat or be eaten," she says in response. Hope you're hungry. If the game's name sounds familiar, that's because it previously popped up via a swiftly-deleted ratings board listing in Brazil . At the time, fans speculated that its name referred to Dread's main antagonist Raven Beak — something now proven correct. It’s eat…or be eaten. #MetroidRavenous . 28/01/2027. Only on #NintendoSwitch2 . pic.twitter.com/b7f9fQWRmo — Nintendo UK (@NintendoUK) September 9, 2026 Metroid Ravenous appears to once again be the work of talented Spanish development studio MercurySteam, the team that previously collaborated with Nintendo for Metroid Dread, as well as Metroid: Samus Returns, the remake of Game Boy title Metroid 2: Return of Samus for 3DS. "A surprise sequel after nearly 20 years, Metroid Dread brings back the legendary exploration and progression and merges it with excellent modern combat and some of the best boss fights ever," we wrote in IGN's Metroid Dread review , scoring it a 9/10. For the uninitiated, Nintendo's side-scrolling Metroid games are narratively separated from its first-person Metroid Prime subseries, though all part of the same overall franchise. Dread and Ravenous sit at the end of the series' chronology to date, years after the events of last year's Metroid Prime 4, so don't expect any direct continuation of that.
